# RLS Doctor

Postgres and Supabase Row Level Security auditor for the command line.

## What it does

Reads catalog metadata and reports RLS risks: disabled RLS on granted tables, unconditional `using (true)` policies, missing `WITH CHECK`, reachable `TRUNCATE`, disabled `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, and broad default privileges. `probe` impersonates application roles in a rolled-back read-only transaction and shows which rows they can actually read.

## Install

```bash
npx rls-doctor check
```

## One command

```bash
rls-doctor check                                    # catalog audit
rls-doctor explain public.profiles                  # one table
rls-doctor probe --app-roles authenticated          # behavioral proof
```

## What it does not do

It never mutates the database. Probe runs inside a rolled-back transaction. It does not call Supabase management APIs and cannot see application-level authorization bugs.

## Limits

Catalog analysis cannot prove runtime authz. Probe results depend on seeded data — empty tables prove nothing.

## For agents

- Skill: `.claude/skills/rls-doctor/SKILL.md` (also `.agents/skills/`)
- MCP: `claude mcp add rls-doctor -- npx -y rls-doctor mcp`
